explain.say: On 10 December 1948, in the Palais de Chaillot in Paris, the United Nations adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, still remembered every year as Human Rights Day. It came three years after the Holocaust and a world war. Look at the timeline of rights claims, from a medieval charter to modern courts.

explain.say: Who wrote it? Look at the network. A committee chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt, with René Cassin of France, P. C. Chang of China, Charles Malik of Lebanon and a first draft by the Canadian John Humphrey. India's Hansa Mehta insisted that Article 1 say all human beings, not all men, are born free and equal. Why did that change matter?

nodes.label: The Declaration
nodes.ask: Who wrote the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?

explain.say: See the vote: 48 states in favour, none against, 8 abstaining, including the Soviet bloc, South Africa and Saudi Arabia, and 2 absent. The Declaration was not a binding treaty but a common standard. Binding covenants followed only in 1966. Why might some governments abstain rather than vote no?

Look at the sorting board. Civil and political rights, like no torture, fair trials and free speech, sit beside economic and social rights, like work, education and health. During the Cold War the West stressed the first group and the Soviet bloc the second, so in 1966 they became two separate treaties. Which group feels more urgent to you?

explain.say: Now the debate. Lynn Hunt traces human rights to eighteenth-century empathy, novels and the declarations of 1776 and 1789. Samuel Moyn argues they became a mass movement only in the 1970s, with Amnesty and the Helsinki accords. Superb work. Challenge: decide which story better explains rights today.

faq.q: Where do human rights come from?
faq.a: Ideas of natural rights developed in the Enlightenment and the American and French revolutions, built on older traditions of law and religion worldwide. After the Second World War the UN set out universal human rights in the 1948 Declaration. Historians such as Lynn Hunt and Samuel Moyn disagree about when they really took hold.

faq.q: Who wrote the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
faq.a: A UN Commission on Human Rights chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt drafted it, with key roles for René Cassin of France, P. C. Chang of China, Charles Malik of Lebanon, Hansa Mehta of India and John Humphrey of Canada, who wrote the first draft. It was adopted on 10 December 1948.
asks: What is the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?

faq.a: Hansa Mehta, India's delegate, argued that the draft's wording all men are born free and equal could exclude women. Article 1 was changed to say all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.

faq.q: When did human rights become important?
faq.a: Samuel Moyn argues that human rights became a powerful international movement only in the 1970s, after other political hopes faded, through groups like Amnesty International, the 1975 Helsinki accords and US President Carter's policies. Others trace a longer history.

A human rights organisation founded in London in 1961 by the lawyer Peter Benenson to campaign for prisoners of conscience, people jailed for their beliefs who have not used violence. It won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

facts: The UN adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on 10 December 1948 in Paris.
The vote was 48 in favour, none against and 8 abstentions.

quiz.say: 48 states voted for the Declaration, 8 abstained and 2 were absent. How many UN members were there?
quiz.why: 48 plus 8 plus 2 equals 58 members in December 1948.
